candidate_070.name: confidence-gated adaptive diversity-to-uncertainty acquisition schedule
candidate_070.mechanism_hypothesis: When a scientific active-learning loop begins with an unreliable model, prioritize coverage/diversity while predictive uncertainty is poorly calibrated, then increase uncertainty-driven acquisition only as global confidence improves; keep batch-level redundancy control separate. This is stronger than a fixed diversity/uncertainty mixture because the reliability of the uncertainty signal changes during the campaign.

primary_evidence.source: Gabriel Dubus, Hugo Magaldi, Anatole Gros-Martial, Adaptive Diversity-Uncertainty Active Learning with Redundancy Control for Bioacoustic Event Classification, BioDCASE 2026 Task 4 technical report / arXiv:2607.04868
primary_evidence.design: Pool-based active learning on fixed PerchV2 bioacoustic embeddings with a fixed classifier/training pipeline, budget 500 labels, batch size 25, 20 acquisition cycles, 5 independent runs. Acquisition score mixes normalized uncertainty and nearest-labelled-point diversity using a global-confidence-dependent coefficient; greedy MMR separately penalizes within-batch redundancy.
primary_evidence.component_result: On BirdSet-HSN, the report directly compares the adaptive schedule against fixed alpha values 0, 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5. The adaptive schedule is reported to outperform all fixed-weight configurations across the learning cycles, with the largest gap early when uncertainty estimates are least reliable. Fixed alpha=0 initially tracks the adaptive method but later saturates while the adaptive schedule continues improving.
primary_evidence.system_result: Across BirdSet plus ATBFL, the technical report reports mean AULC 0.505 for ADU-MMR versus 0.479 CoreSet, 0.422 margin sampling and 0.405 random; best mAP 0.590 versus 0.583/0.532/0.482. Per-dataset AULC was 0.632 on HSN, 0.482 POW, 0.443 UHH and 0.454 ATBFL. The official BioDCASE ranking independently lists ADU-MMR first overall with rank score 0.507; ATBFL is a boundary case where random was slightly better in the report.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This is direct science-domain evidence that a dynamically changing exploration/exploitation weight can beat fixed weights when the trustworthiness of uncertainty changes over time. It supplies the kind of prospective adaptive-vs-fixed comparison missing from candidate_069, albeit for annotation acquisition rather than autonomous experiment selection.
primary_evidence.limits: The fixed-weight component comparison is shown for one BirdSet-HSN subset; the technical report does not provide statistical tests for that figure, tau=0.05 and MMR lambda=0.3 were chosen empirically, and performance advantage disappears on the noisy marine ATBFL domain where the embedding representation is less suitable. This is not an LLM scientist and does not dynamically reallocate separate discovery and coverage lanes under model misspecification, so candidate_070 should not be generalized to open-ended laboratory discovery without further matched evidence.

candidate_070.relation_to_existing: candidate_069 argued that fixed scalar/fixed-ratio mixtures can fail and proposed objective-separated lanes with drift-triggered reallocation. candidate_070 provides a narrower positive control: a confidence-driven adaptive schedule beats fixed uncertainty/diversity weights in a controlled scientific active-learning benchmark. The remaining stronger frontier is separate-lane arbitration using explicit support-drift/generalization diagnostics rather than a single adaptive scalar.
